entries.doc:
ActorEvent is sent by the server when a particular event happens that has to do with an entity. Some of
these events are entity-specific, for example a wolf shaking itself dry, but others are used for each
entity, such as dying.

EventData is optional data associated with a particular event. The data has a different function for
different events, however most events don't use this field at all.
EventType is the ID of the event to be called. It is one of the constants that can be found above.

FireAtPosition is the position in the same world at which the event should fire. If this is not present,
the position entity will be used instead.

EntityRuntimeID is the runtime ID of the entity. The runtime ID is unique for each world session, and
entities are generally identified in packets using this runtime ID.
EntityLink is a link between two entities, typically being one entity riding another.

Immediate is set to immediately dismount an entity from another. This should be set when the mount of
an entity is killed.

RiderInitiated specifies if the link was created by the rider, for example the player starting to ride
a horse by itself. This is generally true in vanilla environment for players.

RiddenEntityUniqueID is the entity unique ID of the entity that is being ridden. For a player sitting
in a boat, this is the unique ID of the boat.

RiderEntityUniqueID is the entity unique ID of the entity that is riding. For a player sitting in a
boat, this is the unique ID of the player.
Type is one of the types above. It specifies the way the entity is linked to another entity.
VehicleAngularVelocity is the angular velocity of the vehicle that the rider is riding.

ActorPickRequest is sent by the client when it tries to pick an entity, so that it gets a spawn egg which
can spawn that entity.

EntityUniqueID is the unique ID of the entity that was attempted to be picked. The server must find the
type of that entity and provide the correct spawn egg to the player.

HotBarSlot is the held hot bar slot of the player at the time of trying to pick the entity. If empty,
the resulting spawn egg should be put into this slot.
WithData is true if the pick request requests the entity metadata.

AddActor is sent by the server to the client to spawn an entity to the player. It is used for every entity
except other players, for which the AddPlayer packet is used.

EntityLinks is a list of entity links that are currently active on the entity. These links alter the
way the entity shows up when first spawned in terms of it shown as riding an entity. Setting these
links is important for new viewers to see the entity is riding another entity.

EntityType is the string entity type of the entity, for example 'minecraft:skeleton'. A list of these
entities may be found online.

Attributes is a slice of attributes that the entity has. It includes attributes such as its health,
movement speed, etc.

Position is the position to spawn the entity on. If the entity is on a distance that the player cannot
see it, the entity will still show up if the player moves closer.

EntityUniqueID is the unique ID of the entity. The unique ID is a value that remains consistent across
different sessions of the same world, but most servers simply fill the runtime ID of the entity out for
this field.

EntityRuntimeID is the runtime ID of the entity. The runtime ID is unique for each world session, and
entities are generally identified in packets using this runtime ID.

Velocity is the initial velocity the entity spawns with. This velocity will initiate client side
movement of the entity.

AddBehaviourTree is sent by the server to the client. The packet is currently unused by both client and
server.
BehaviourTree is an unused string.

AddItemActor is sent by the server to the client to make an item entity show up. It is one of the few
entities that cannot be sent using the AddActor packet

EntityMetadata is a map of entity metadata, which includes flags and data properties that alter in
particular the way the entity looks. Flags include ones such as 'on fire' and 'sprinting'.
The metadata values are indexed by their property key.

FromFishing specifies if the item was obtained by fishing it up using a fishing rod. It is not clear
why the client needs to know this.

Item is the item that is spawned. It must have a valid ID for it to show up client-side. If it is not
a valid item, the client will crash when coming near.

Position is the position to spawn the entity on. If the entity is on a distance that the player cannot
see it, the entity will still show up if the player moves closer.

EntityUniqueID is the unique ID of the entity. The unique ID is a value that remains consistent across
different sessions of the same world, but most servers simply fill the runtime ID of the entity out for
this field.

EntityRuntimeID is the runtime ID of the entity. The runtime ID is unique for each world session, and
entities are generally identified in packets using this runtime ID.

Velocity is the initial velocity the entity spawns with. This velocity will initiate client side
movement of the entity.

AddPainting is sent by the server to the client to make a painting entity show up. It is one of the few
entities that cannot be sent using the AddActor packet.
Direction is the facing direction of the painting.

Title is the title of the painting. It specifies the motive of the painting. The title of the painting
must be valid.

Position is the position to spawn the entity on. If the entity is on a distance that the player cannot
see it, the entity will still show up if the player moves closer.

EntityUniqueID is the unique ID of the entity. The unique ID is a value that remains consistent across
different sessions of the same world, but most servers simply fill the runtime ID of the entity out for
this field.

EntityRuntimeID is the runtime ID of the entity. The runtime ID is unique for each world session, and
entities are generally identified in packets using this runtime ID.

AddPlayer is sent by the server to the client to make a player entity show up client-side. It is one of the
few entities that cannot be sent using the AddActor packet.

EntityLinks is a list of entity links that are currently active on the player. These links alter the
way the player shows up when first spawned in terms of it shown as riding an entity. Setting these
links is important for new viewers to see the player is riding another entity.

BuildPlatform is the build platform/device OS of the player that is about to be added, as it sent in
the Login packet when joining.

DeviceID is the device ID set in one of the files found in the storage of the device of the player. It
may be changed freely, so it should not be relied on for anything.

PlatformChatID is an identifier only set for particular platforms when chatting (presumably only for
Nintendo Switch). It is otherwise an empty string, and is used to decide which players are able to
chat with each other.
GameType is the game type of the player. If set to GameTypeSpectator, the player will not be shown to viewers.

Position is the position to spawn the player on. If the player is on a distance that the viewer cannot
see it, the player will still show up if the viewer moves closer.

EntityRuntimeID is the runtime ID of the player. The runtime ID is unique for each world session, and
entities are generally identified in packets using this runtime ID.

UUID is the UUID of the player. It is the same UUID that the client sent in the Login packet at the
start of the session. A player with this UUID must exist in the player list (built up using the
PlayerList packet), for it to show up in-game.

Velocity is the initial velocity the player spawns with. This velocity will initiate client side
movement of the player.
AddVolumeEntity sends a volume entity's definition and metadata from server to client.
EngineVersion is the engine version the entity is using, for example, '1.17.0'.
AutoJump is a boolean indicating whether the player is allowed to jump automatically or not.
ImmutableWorld is a boolean indicating whether the player is allowed to modify the world or not.
ShowNameTags is a boolean indicating whether player name tags are shown or not.

NoMvP is a boolean indicating whether mobs are allowed to fight the player or not. It is unclear why this is sent
to the client.
NoPvM is a boolean indicating whether the player is allowed to fight mobs or not.

AgentAction is an Education Edition packet sent from the server to the client to return a response to a
previously requested action.
Action represents the action type that was requested. It is one of the constants defined above.
Identifier is a JSON identifier referenced in the initial action.
Response is a JSON string containing the response to the action.
AgentAnimation is an Education Edition packet sent from the server to the client to make an agent perform an animation.

Animation is the ID of the animation that the agent should perform. As of its implementation, there are no IDs
that can be used in the regular client.

EntityRuntimeID is the runtime ID of the entity. The runtime ID is unique for each world session, and
entities are generally identified in packets using this runtime ID.

AnimateEntity is sent by the server to animate an entity client-side. It may be used to play a single
animation, or to activate a controller which can start a sequence of animations based on different
conditions specified in an animation controller.
Much of the documentation of this packet can be found at
https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/minecraft/creator/reference/content/animationsreference
MAnimation is the name of a single animation to start playing.
MBlendOutTime does not currently seem to be used.

MController is the animation controller that is used to manage animations. These controllers decide when
to play which animation.

MNextState is the first state to start with. These states are declared in animation controllers (which,
in themselves, are animations too). These states in turn may have animations and transitions to move to
a next state.
MRuntimeIds is list of runtime IDs of entities that the animation should be applied to.
MStopExpression is a MoLang expression that specifies when the animation should be stopped.
MStopExpressionVersion is the MoLang stop condition version.

Animate is sent by the server to send a player animation from one player to all viewers of that player. It
is used for a couple of actions, such as arm swimming and critical hits.

ActionType is the ID of the animation action to execute. It is one of the action type constants that
may be found above.
Data ...

SwingSource is the source for swing actions. It is one of the action type constants that
may be found above.

EntityRuntimeID is the runtime ID of the player that the animation should be played upon. The runtime
ID is unique for each world session, and entities are generally identified in packets using this
runtime ID.

AnvilDamage is sent by the client to request the dealing damage to an anvil. This packet is completely
pointless and the server should never listen to it.
BlockPosition is the position in the world that the anvil can be found at.
PlayerArmourDamageEntry represents an entry for a single piece of armour that should be damaged.
ArmourSlot is the index of the armour slot to damage.
Damage is the amount of damage to apply to the armour in the specified slot.
ArrowShape represents an arrow debug shape.
ArrowEndLocation is the arrow end location of the shape.
ArrowHeadLength is the arrow head length of the shape.
ArrowHeadRadius is the arrow head radius of the shape.
Segments is the segments that used for the debug arrow's head.
AttributeData represents a polymorphic attribute value.
AttributeLayerSettings represents settings for an attribute layer.
AttributeLayerData represents a complete attribute layer.
EnvironmentAttributeData represents an environment attribute with optional transition data.

AttributeModifier temporarily buffs/debuffs a given attribute until the modifier is used. In vanilla, these are
mainly used for effects.
Amount is the amount of difference between the current value of the attribute and the new value.
ID is the unique ID of the modifier. It is used to identify the modifier in the packet.

IsSerializable ...
TODO: Figure out what this field is used for.
Name is the name of the attribute that is modified.

Operand ...
TODO: Figure out what this field is used for.

Operation is the operation that is performed on the attribute. It can be addition, multiply base, multiply total
or cap.

AutomationClientConnect is used to make the client connect to a websocket server. This websocket server has
the ability to execute commands on the behalf of the client and it can listen for certain events fired by
the client.

AvailableActorIdentifiers is sent by the server at the start of the game to let the client know all
entities that are available on the server.

AvailableCommands is sent by the server to send a list of all commands that
the player is able to use on the server. This packet holds all the arguments
of each commands as well, making it possible for the client to provide
auto-completion and command usages. AvailableCommands packets can be resent,
but the packet is often very big, so doing this very often should be avoided.

ChainedSubcommandData is a slice of all subcommands that are followed by a chained command. An example usage of this
is /execute which allows you to run another command as another entity or at a different position etc.

ChainedSubcommandValues is a slice of all chained subcommand names. ChainedSubcommandValues generally should
contain each possible value only once. ChainedSubcommands are built by pointing to entries in this slice.

Commands is a list of all commands that the client should show
client-side. The AvailableCommands packet replaces any commands sent
before. It does not only add the commands that are sent in it.

Constraints is a list of constraints that should be applied to certain
options of enums in the commands above.

EnumData is a slice of all (fixed) command enums present in any of the
commands.

EnumValues is a slice of all enum values of any enum in the
AvailableCommands packet. EnumValues generally should contain each
possible value only once. Enums are built by pointing to entries in this
slice.

PostFixes, like EnumValues, is a slice of all suffix values of any command
parameter in the AvailableCommands packet.

SoftEnums is a slice of dynamic command enums. These command enums can
be changed during runtime without having to resend an AvailableCommands
packet.

ChainedSubcommand represents a subcommand that can have chained commands, such as /execute which allows you to run
another command as another entity or at a different position etc.
Name is the name of the chained subcommand and shows up in the list as a regular subcommand enum.
SubCommandValues contains the index and parameter type of the chained subcommand.
ChainedSubcommandValue represents the value for a chained subcommand argument.

SubCommandFirstValue is the index of the argument in the ChainedSubcommandValues slice from the AvailableCommands packet. This is
then used to set the type specified by the Value field below.

SubCommandSecondValue is a combination of the flags above and specified the type of argument. Unlike regular parameter types,
this should NOT contain any of the special flags (valid, enum, suffixed or soft enum) but only the basic types.

CommandEnumConstraint is sent in the AvailableCommands packet to limit what values of an enum may be used
taking in account things such as whether cheats are enabled.
ConstraintIndices holds a slice of constraints as present in the constants above.

EnumSymbol points to an enum in the AvailableCommands packet to which this
constraint should apply to.

EnumValueSymbol points to an enum value in the AvailableCommands packet that this
constraint should apply to.

CommandEnum represents an enum in a command usage. The enum typically has a type and a set of options that
are valid. A value that is not one of the options results in a failure during execution.

Name is the type of the command enum. The type will show up in the command usage as the type of the
argument if it has a certain amount of arguments, or when Options is set to true in the
command holding the enum.

Values holds a list of indices that point to the EnumValues slice in the
AvailableCommandsPacket. These represent the options of the enum.

CommandOverload represents an overload of a command. This overload can be compared to function overloading
in languages such as java. It represents a single usage of the command. A command may have multiple
different overloads, which are handled differently.

ParameterData is a list of command parameters that are part of the overload. These parameters specify the
usage of the command when this overload is applied.
IsChaining determines if the parameters use chained subcommands or not.

CommandParameter represents a single parameter of a command overload, which accepts a certain type of input
values. It has a name and a type which show up client-side when a player is entering the command.

Optional specifies if the command parameter is optional to enter. Note that no non-optional parameter
should ever be present in a command overload after an optional parameter. When optional, the parameter
shows up like so: [$Name: $Type], whereas when mandatory, it shows up like so: <$Name: $Type>.

Name is the name of the command parameter. It shows up in the usage like <$Name: $Type>, with the
exception of enum types, which show up simply as a list of options if the list is short enough and
Options is set to false.

Options holds a combinations of options that additionally apply to the command parameter. The list of
options can be found above.

Type is a rather odd combination of type(flag)s that result in a certain parameter type to show up
client-side. It is a combination of the flags above. The basic types must be combined with the
ArgumentTypeFlagBasic flag (and integers with a suffix ArgumentTypeFlagSuffixed), whereas enums are
combined with the ArgumentTypeFlagEnum flag.

DynamicEnum is an enum variant that can have its options changed during runtime,
without sending a new AvailableCommands packet.

EnumName is the type of the command enum. The type will show up in the command usage as the type of the
argument if it has a certain amount of arguments, or when Options is set to true in the
command holding the enum.
EnumOptions is a slice of possible options for the enum.
AwardAchievement is sent by the server to award an achievement to a player.

AchievementID is the ID of the achievement that should be awarded to the player. The values for these
IDs are currently unknown.
DataStoreChange represents a change to a data store property value.
DataStoreName is the name of the data store.
Property is the property that changed.
NewValue is the new property value.
UpdateCount is the update count.
WhiskerScopeDataSummary represents a whisker profiler scope diagnostic summary.
Indentation is the indentation string of the whisker scope within the profiler hierarchy.
Label is the label of the whisker scope.
TotalHighCostNS is the total time, in nanoseconds, spent in the high-cost portion of the scope.
TotalLowCostNS is the total time, in nanoseconds, spent in the low-cost portion of the scope.
TotalMidCostNS is the total time, in nanoseconds, spent in the mid-cost portion of the scope.
BiomeCappedSurface specifies the materials to use for the capped surface of a biome, such as in the Nether.
BeachBlock is an optional runtime ID to use for the beach block.
CeilingBlocks is a list of runtime IDs to use for the ceiling blocks.
FloorBlocks is a list of runtime IDs to use for the floor blocks.
FoundationBlock is an optional runtime ID to use for the foundation block.
SeaBlock is an optional runtime ID to use for the sea block.
BiomeClimate represents the climate of a biome, mainly for ambience but also defines certain behaviours.
Downfall is the amount that precipitation affects colours and block changes.

SnowAccumulationMax is the maximum amount of snow that can accumulate in the biome, every 0.125 is
another layer of snow.

SnowAccumulationMin is the minimum amount of snow that can accumulate in the biome, every 0.125 is
another layer of snow.
Temperature is the temperature of the biome, used for weather, biome behaviours and sky colour.
BiomeConditionalTransformation is the legacy method of transforming biomes.
ConditionJSON is an index of the condition JSON data in the string list.

MinPassingNeighbours is the minimum number of neighbours that must pass the condition for the
transformation to be applied.
WeightedBiomes is a list of biomes and their weights.
BiomeConsolidatedFeature represents a feature that is consolidated into a single feature for the biome.
CanUseInternal is true if the feature can use internal features.
Feature is the index of the feature's name in the string list.
Identifier is the index of the feature's identifier in the string list.
Pass is the index of the feature's pass in the string list.
Scatter defines how the feature is scattered in the biome.
BiomeCoordinate specifies coordinate rules for where features can be scattered in the biome.

Distribution is the type of distribution to use for the coordinate, and is one of the
BiomeRandomDistributionType constants above.
GridOffset is the offset of the grid, used for fixed grid and jittered grid distributions.
GridStepSize is the step size of the grid, used for fixed grid and jittered grid distributions.
MaxValue is the index of the maximum value expression in the string list.
MaxValueType is the type of expression operation to use for the maximum value, and is one of the
MinValue is the index of the minimum value expression in the string list.

MinValueType is the type of expression operation to use for the minimum value, and is one of the
BiomeExpressionOp constants above.

BiomeDefinition represents a biome definition in the game. This can be a vanilla biome or a completely
custom biome.
Depth is the depth of the biome.
Downfall is the amount that precipitation affects colours and block changes.
FoliageSnow is the progression factor for foliage turning white due to snow.
Rain is true if the biome has rain, false if it is a dry biome.
Scale is the scale of the biome.

Tags are a list of indices of tags in the string list. These are used to group biomes together for
biome generation and other purposes.
Temperature is the temperature of the biome, used for weather, biome behaviours and sky colour.

BiomeDefinitionList is sent by the server to let the client know all biomes that are available and
implemented on the server side. When enabled, it also includes information for the client to
accurately recreate the server-side generation in vanilla worlds/servers for increased performance.

StringList is a makeshift dictionary implementation Mojang created to try and reduce the size of the
overall packet. It is a list of common strings that are used in the biome definitions, such as
biome names, float values or query expressions.
BiomeElementData are set rules to adjust the surface materials of the biome.
AdjustedMaterials is the materials to use for the surface layers of the biome if selected.
HeightMax is the index of the maximum height expression in the string list.

HeightMaxType is the type of expression operation to use for the maximum height, and is one of the
BiomeExpressionOp constants above.
HeightMin is the index of the minimum height expression in the string list.

HeightMinType is the type of expression operation to use for the minimum height, and is one of the
BiomeExpressionOp constants above.
NoiseFrequencyScale is the frequency scale of the noise used to adjust the surface materials.
NoiseLowerBound is the minimum noise value required to be selected.
NoiseUpperBound is the maximum noise value required to be selected.
BiomeMesaSurface specifies the materials to use for the mesa biome.
BrycePillars is true if the biome has bryce pillars, which are tall spire-like structures.
ClayMaterial is the runtime ID of the block to use for clay layers.
HardClayMaterial is the runtime ID of the block to use for hard clay layers.
HasForest is true if the biome has a forest.
BiomeMountainParameters specifies the parameters for a mountain biome.
EastSlopes is true if the biome has east slopes.
NorthSlopes is true if the biome has north slopes.
SouthSlopes is true if the biome has south slopes.
SteepBlock is the runtime ID of the block to use for steep slopes.
TopSlideEnabled is true if the biome has top slide enabled.
WestSlopes is true if the biome has west slopes.

BiomeMultiNoiseRules specifies the rules for multi-noise biomes, which are biomes that are defined by
multiple noise parameters instead of just temperature and humidity.
Altitude is the altitude level of the biome.
Humidity is the humidity level of the biome.
Temperature is the temperature level of the biome.
Weight is the weight of the biome, with a higher weight being more likely to be selected.
Weirdness is the weirdness level of the biome.
BiomeNoiseGradientSurface specifies noise-gradient surface block data for a biome.
GradientBlocks is a list of noise block specifiers used by the gradient.
Noise is the noise descriptor used by the gradient.
NonReplaceableBlocks is a list of block runtime IDs that may not be replaced.
BiomeReplacementData represents data for biome replacements.
Amount is the amount of replacement to apply.
Dimension is the dimension ID where the replacement applies.
NoiseFrequencyScale ...
Biome is the biome ID to replace.
ReplacementIndex is the index of the replacement.
TargetBiomes is a list of target biome IDs for the replacement.
ChanceDenominator is the denominator of the chance expression.
ChanceNumerator is the numerator of the chance expression.
ChangePercent is the index of the chance expression in the string list.

ChancePercentType is the type of expression operation to use for the chance percent, and is one of the
BiomeExpressionOp constants above.
Coordinates is a list of coordinate rules to scatter the feature within.

EvaluationOrder is the order in which the coordinates are evaluated, and is one of the
CoordinateEvaluationOrder constants above.
Iterations is the index of the iterations expression in the string list.

IterationsType is the type of expression operation to use for the iterations, and is one of the
BiomeExpressionOp constants above.
BiomeSurfaceBuilder specifies the materials and special surface rules to use for a biome surface.
CappedSurface is optional information to specify the biome's capped surface, i.e. in the Nether.
HasDefaultOverworldSurface is true if the biome has a default overworld surface.
HasFrozenOceanSurface is true if the biome has a frozen ocean surface.
HasSwampSurface is true if the biome has a swamp surface.
HasTheEndSurface is true if the biome has an end surface.
MesaSurface is optional information to specify the biome's mesa surface.
NoiseGradientSurface is optional information to specify noise-gradient surface data.
SurfaceMaterials is a set of materials to use for the surface layers of the biome.
BiomeSurfaceMaterial specifies the materials to use for the surface layers of the biome.
FoundationBlock is the runtime ID to use for the foundation layers.
MidBlock is the runtime ID to use for the middle layers.
SeaBlock is the runtime ID to use for the sea layers.
SeaFloorBlock is the runtime ID to use for the sea floor.
SeaFloorDepth is the depth of the sea floor, in blocks.
TopBlock is the runtime ID of the block to use for the top layer.
BiomeTemperatureWeight defines the weight for a temperature, used for weighted randomness.
Temperature is the temperature that can be selected.
Weight is the weight of the temperature, with a higher weight being more likely to be selected.

BlockActorData is sent by the server to update data of a block entity client-side, for example the data of
a chest.

Position is the position of the block that holds the block entity. If no block entity is at this
position, the packet is ignored by the client.

BlockEvent is sent by the server to initiate a certain event that has something to do with blocks in
specific, for example opening a chest.
BlockPosition is the position of the block that an event occurred at.

EventType is the type of the block event. The event type decides the way the event data that follows
is used. It is one of the constants found above.

EventValue holds event type specific data. For chests for example, opening the chest means the data must
hold 1, whereas closing it should hold 0.

BlockPickRequest is sent by the client when it requests to pick a block in the world and place its item in
their inventory.
HotBarSlot is the slot that was held at the time of picking a block.

Position is the position at which the client requested to pick the block. The block at that position
should have its item put in HotBarSlot if it is empty.

AddBlockNBT specifies if the item should get all NBT tags from the block, meaning the item places a
block practically always equal to the one picked.

BlockPos is the position of a block. It is composed of three integers, and is typically written as either
3 varint32s or a varint32, varuint32 and varint32.

BlockPos is the position of a block. It is composed of three integers, and is typically written as either
3 varint32s or a varint32, varuint32 and varint32.

BookEdit is sent by the client when it edits a book. It is sent each time a modification was made and the
player stops its typing 'session', rather than simply after closing the book.

BossEvent is sent by the server to make a specific 'boss event' occur in the
world. It includes features such as showing a boss bar to the player and
turning the sky dark.

Colour is the colour of the boss bar that is shown when a player is
subscribed. It is one of the BossEventColour constants listed above.
EventType is the type of the event. It is one of the BossEvent constants above.

FilteredBossBarTitle is a filtered version of BossBarTitle with all the
profanity removed. The client will use this over BossBarTitle if this
field is not empty and they have the "Filter Profanity" setting enabled.

HealthPercentage is the percentage of health that is shown in the boss
bar (0.0-1.0). The HealthPercentage may be set to a specific value if the
BossEntityUniqueID matches the client's entity unique ID.

BossBarTitle is the title shown above the boss bar. It may be set to set
a different title if the BossEntityUniqueID matches the client's entity
unique ID.

Overlay is the overlay of the boss bar that is shown on top of the boss
bar when a player is subscribed. It is one of the BossEventOverlay
constants listed above.

BossEntityUniqueID is the unique ID of the boss entity that the boss
event sent involves. By default, the health percentage and title of the
boss bar depend on the health and name tag of this entity. If
BossEntityUniqueID is the same as the client's entity unique ID, its
HealthPercentage and BossBarTitle can be freely altered.
CameraAimAssistActorPriorityData represents priority data for aim assist actor targeting.
ActorIndex is the index of the actor.
CategoryIndex is the index of the aim assist category.
PresetIndex is the index of the aim assist preset.
PriorityValue is the priority value for this actor.
CameraAimAssistActorPriority is sent by the server to define actor-specific aim assist priorities.
CameraAimAssistActorPriorityList is a list of aim assist actor priority entries.
CameraAimAssist is sent by the server to the client to set up aim assist for the client's camera.
Action is the action that should be performed with the aim assist. This is one of the constants above.

Distance is the maximum distance from the player's cursor should check for a target, if TargetMode is
set to protocol.AimAssistTargetModeDistance.
PresetID is the ID of the preset that has previously been defined in the CameraAimAssistPresets packet.
ShowDebugRender specifies if debug render should be shown.

TargetMode is the mode that the camera should use for detecting targets. This is currently one of
protocol.AimAssistTargetModeAngle or protocol.AimAssistTargetModeDistance.

ViewAngle is the maximum angle around the playes's cursor that the aim assist should check for a target,
if TargetMode is set to protocol.AimAssistTargetModeAngle.

CameraAimAssistPresets is sent by the server to the client to provide a list of categories and presets
that can be used when sending a CameraAimAssist packet or a CameraInstruction including aim assist.
CameraAimAssistCategories is a list of presets which define a base for how aim assist should behave
CameraAimAssistPresets is a list of categories which can be referenced by one of the Presets.
Operation is the operation to perform with the presets. It is one of the constants above.
AttachToEntity is the entity ID to attach the camera to.
Clear can be set to true to clear all the current camera instructions.
DetachFromEntity can be set to true to detach the camera from the current entity.
Fade is a camera instruction that fades the screen to a specified colour.
FieldOfView is a camera instruction that updates the field of view for the camera.
RemoveTarget can be set to true to remove the current aim assist target.
Set is a camera instruction that sets the camera to a specified preset.
Spline is a camera instruction that creates a spline path for the camera to follow.
Target is a camera instruction that targets a specific entity.
CameraInstructionTarget represents a camera instruction that targets a specific entity.
EntityUniqueID is the unique ID of the entity that the camera should target.
CameraInstructionFade represents a camera instruction that fades the screen to a specified colour.
Color is the colour of the screen to fade to. This only uses the red, green and blue components.

Time is the time data for the fade, which includes the fade in duration, wait duration and fade out
duration.
CameraFadeTimeData represents the time data for a CameraInstructionFade.
FadeInTime is the time in seconds for the screen to fully fade in.
FadeOutTime is the time in seconds for the screen to fully fade out.
HoldTime is time in seconds to wait before fading out.
CameraInstructionFieldOfView represents a camera instruction that updates the field of view.
EaseTime is the time in seconds that the easing function should take.
FieldOfView is the field of view of the camera.
Clear can be set to true to clear the current instruction.

CameraInstructionSet represents a camera instruction that sets the camera to a specified preset and can be extended
with easing functions and translations to the camera's position and rotation.
Default determines whether the camera is a default camera or not.
Ease represents the easing function that is used by the instruction.
EntityOffset is an offset from the entity that the camera should be rendered at.
Facing is a vector that the camera will always face towards during the duration of the instruction.
Pos represents the position of the camera.
Preset is the index of the preset in the CameraPresets packet sent to the player.
RemoveIgnoreStartingValuesComponent behavior is currently unknown.
Rot represents the rotation of the camera.

ViewOffset is an offset based on a pivot point to the player, causing the camera to be shifted in a
certain direction.
CameraEase represents an easing function that can be used by a CameraInstructionSet.
Time is the time in seconds that the easing function should take.
Type is the type of easing function used. This is one of the constants above.
CameraSplineInstruction represents a camera instruction that creates a spline path for the camera to follow.
Curve is a list of points that define the spline curve.
LoadFromJSON optionally determines whether the spline should be loaded from a JSON definition.
ProgressKeyFrames is a list of progress key frames for the spline.
RotationOptions is a list of rotation options for the spline.
SplineIdentifier is an optional identifier for referencing the spline by name.
TotalTime is the total time for the spline animation.
CameraProgressOption represents a progress keyframe option for camera spline instructions.
Time is the time for this progress option.
Value is the progress value.
CameraRotationOption represents a rotation option for camera spline instructions.
Time is the time for this rotation option.
Value is the rotation value.
CameraInstructionTarget represents a camera instruction that targets a specific entity.
TargetActorID is the unique ID of the entity that the camera should target.
TargetCenterOffset is the offset from the center of the entity that the camera should target.
CameraInstruction gives a custom camera specific instructions to operate.

Camera is sent by the server to use an Education Edition camera on a player. It produces an image
client-side.
CameraEntityUniqueID is the unique ID of the camera entity from which the picture was taken.

TargetPlayerUniqueID is the unique ID of the target player. The unique ID is a value that remains
consistent across different sessions of the same world, but most servers simply fill the runtime ID of
the player out for this field.

Presets is a list of camera presets that can be used by other cameras. The order of this list is important because
the index of presets is used as a pointer in the CameraInstruction packet.
CameraPresets gives the client a list of custom camera presets.

CameraShake is sent by the server to make the camera shake client-side. This feature was added for map-
making partners.

Intensity is the intensity of the shaking. The client limits this value to 4, so anything higher may
not work.
Duration is the number of seconds the camera will shake for.

Action is the action to be performed, and is one of the constants listed above. Currently the
different actions will either add or stop shaking the client.

Type is the type of shake, and is one of the constants listed above. The different type affects how
the shake looks in game.
CameraSpline is sent by the server to define camera spline paths.
CameraDataSplines is a list of camera spline definitions.

ChangeDimension is sent by the server to the client to send a dimension change screen client-side. Once the
screen is cleared client-side, the client will send a PlayerAction packet with
PlayerActionDimensionChangeDone.

LoadingScreenID is a unique ID for the loading screen that the player is currently in. The client will
update the server on its state through the ServerBoundLoadingScreen packet, and it can be used to not
send specific packets to the client if it is changing dimensions. This field should be unique for every
ChangeDimension packet sent.
Position is the position in the new dimension that the player is spawned in.

Respawn specifies if the dimension change was respawn based, meaning that the player died in one
dimension and got respawned into another. The client will send a PlayerAction packet with
PlayerActionDimensionChangeRequest if it dies in another dimension, indicating that it needs a
DimensionChange packet with Respawn set to true.
ChangeMobProperty is a packet sent from the server to the client to change one of the properties of a mob client-side.
EntityUniqueID is the unique ID of the entity whose property is being changed.
BoolValue is set if the property value is a bool type. If the type is not a bool, this field is ignored.
FloatValue is set if the property value is a float type. If the type is not a float, this field is ignored.
IntValue is set if the property value is an int type. If the type is not an int, this field is ignored.
Property is the name of the property being updated.
StringValue is set if the property value is a string type. If the type is not a string, this field is ignored.
ChunkPos is the position of a chunk. It is composed of two integers and is written as two varint32s.

ChunkRadiusUpdated is sent by the server in response to a RequestChunkRadius packet. It defines the chunk
radius that the server allows the client to have. This may be lower than the chunk radius requested by the
client in the RequestChunkRadius packet.

ChunkRadius is the final chunk radius that the client will adapt when it receives the packet. It does
not have to be the same as the requested chunk radius.

ClientCacheBlobStatus is part of the blob cache protocol. It is sent by the client to let the server know
what blobs it needs and which blobs it already has, in an ACK type system.

FoundIds is a list of blob hashes that the client has a blob available for. The blobs hashes here mean
that the client already has them: The server does not need to send the blobs anymore.

MissingIds is a list of blob hashes that the client does not have a blob available for. The server
should send the blobs matching these hashes as soon as possible.

ClientCacheMissResponse is part of the blob cache protocol. It is sent by the server in response to a
ClientCacheBlobStatus packet and contains the blob data of all blobs that the client acknowledged not to
have yet.

MissingBlobs is a list of all blobs that the client sent misses for in the ClientCacheBlobStatus. These blobs
hold the data of the blobs with the hashes they are matched with.

ClientCacheStatus is sent by the client to the server at the start of the game. It is sent to let the
server know if it supports the client-side blob cache. Clients such as Nintendo Switch do not support the
cache, and attempting to use it anyway will fail.

IsCacheSupported specifies if the blob cache is enabled. If false, the server should not attempt to use the
blob cache. If true, it may do so, but it may also choose not to use it.

ClientCameraAimAssist is sent by the server to send a player animation from one player to all viewers of that player. It
is used for a couple of actions, such as arm swimming and critical hits.
Action is the action to perform with the aim assist. It is one of the constants above.
AllowAimAssist specifies the client can use aim assist or not.

CameraPresetID is the identifier of the preset to use which was previously defined in the CameraAimAssistPresets
packet.

ClientMovementPredictionSync is sent by the client to the server periodically if the client has received
movement corrections from the server, containing information about client-predictions that are relevant
to movement.
EntityUniqueID is the unique ID of the entity that the prediction data applies to.

ClientToServerHandshake is sent by the client in response to a ServerToClientHandshake packet sent by the
server. It is the first encrypted packet in the login handshake and serves as a confirmation that
encryption is correctly initialised client side.
ClientBoundAttributeLayerSync is sent by the server to synchronise attribute layers with the client.

ClientBoundCloseForm is sent by the server to clear the entire form stack of the client. This means that all
forms that are currently open will be closed. This does not affect inventories and other containers.

ClientBoundControlSchemeSet is sent by the server upon the client's request or the usage of the vanilla
/controlscheme command. It is used to set the control scheme of the client, often used in combination with
custom cameras.

ControlScheme is the control scheme that the client should use. It is one of the following:
 - ControlSchemeLockedPlayerRelativeStrafe is the default behaviour, this cannot be set when the client
   is in a custom camera.
 - ControlSchemeCameraRelative makes movement relative to the camera's transform, with the client's
   rotation being relative to the client's movement.
 - ControlSchemeCameraRelativeStrafe makes movement relative to the camera's transform, with the
   client's rotation being locked.
 - ControlSchemePlayerRelative makes movement relative to the player's transform, meaning holding
   left/right will make the player turn in a circle.
 - ControlSchemePlayerRelativeStrafe makes movement the same as the default behaviour, but can be
   used in a custom camera.

ClientBoundDataDrivenUICloseScreen is sent by the server to close a data-driven UI screen on the client.
If FormID is not set, all data-driven UI screens are closed.
FormID is the optional unique instance ID of the form to close. If not set, all forms are closed.
ClientBoundDataDrivenUIReload is sent by the server to reload the data-driven UI on the client.
ClientBoundDataDrivenUIShowScreen is sent by the server to show a data-driven UI screen on the client.
DataInstanceID is an optional data ID associated with the screen.
FormID is a unique instance ID for the form, used for scripting to identify specific screen instances.
ScreenID is the identifier of the screen to show.
ClientBoundDataStore is sent by the server to update, change or remove data store entries on the client.
Updates is an array of data store changes. Each entry has its own change type discriminator.
ClientBoundDebugRenderer is sent by the server to spawn an outlined cube on client-side.
Type is the type of action. It is one of the constants above.

ClientBoundMapItemData is sent by the server to the client to update the data of a map shown to the client.
It is sent with a combination of flags that specify what data is updated.
The ClientBoundMapItemData packet may be used to update specific parts of the map only. It is not required
to send the entire map each time when updating one part.

MapsIncludedIn holds an array of map IDs that the map updated is included in. This has to do with the
scale of the map: Each map holds its own map ID and all map IDs of maps that include this map and have
a bigger scale. This means that a scale 0 map will have 5 map IDs in this slice, whereas a scale 4 map
will have only 1 (its own).
The actual use of this field remains unknown.

Decorations is a list of fixed decorations located on the map. The decorations will not change
client-side, unless the server updates them.

Dimension is the dimension of the map that should be updated, for example the overworld (0), the nether
(1) or the end (2).

Height is the height of the texture area that was updated. The height may be a subset of the total
height of the map.

LockedMap specifies if the map that was updated was a locked map, which may be done using a cartography
table.

MapID is the unique identifier that represents the map that is updated over network. It remains
consistent across sessions.
Origin is the center position of the map being updated.
Pixels is a list of pixel colours for the new texture of the map. It is indexed as Pixels[y*height + x].
Scale is the scale of the map as it is shown in-game.

XOffset is the X offset in pixels at which the updated texture area starts. From this X, the updated
texture will extend exactly Width pixels to the right.

YOffset is the Y offset in pixels at which the updated texture area starts. From this Y, the updated
texture will extend exactly Height pixels up.

TrackedObjects is a list of tracked objects on the map, which may either be entities or blocks. The
client makes sure these tracked objects are actually tracked. (position updated etc.)

Width is the width of the texture area that was updated. The width may be a subset of the total width
of the map.
ClientBoundTextureShift is sent by the server to control texture shift animations on the client.
ActionID is the texture shift action to perform. It is one of the constants above.
AllSteps is a list of all steps in the texture shift.
CollectionName is the name of the texture shift collection.
CurrentLengthTicks is the current length of the shift in ticks.
Enabled specifies if the texture shift is enabled.
FromStep is the step to shift from.
ToStep is the step to shift to.
TotalLengthTicks is the total length of the shift in ticks.
ClientboundUpdateSoundData updates a playing sound by its server handle. The event starts with one byte selecting the update, followed by that update's payload.
ServerSoundHandle is the server-side handle of the sound to update.

CodeBuilder is an Education Edition packet sent by the server to the client to open the URL to a Code
Builder (websocket) server.

ShouldOpenCodeBuilder specifies if the client should automatically open the Code Builder app. If set to
true, the client will attempt to use the Code Builder app to connect to and interface with the server
running at the URL above.
URL is the url to the Code Builder (websocket) server.

CodeBuilderSource is an Education Edition packet sent by the client to the server to run an operation with a
code builder.

Category is used to distinguish the category of the operation performed. It is always one of the constants
listed above.
CodeStatus is the status of the code builder. It is always one of the constants listed above.
Operation is used to distinguish the operation performed. It is always one of the constants listed above.

CommandBlockUpdate is sent by the client to update a command block at a specific position. The command
block may be either a physical block or an entity.

Command is the command currently entered in the command block. This is the command that is executed
when the command block is activated.

ExecuteOnFirstTick specifies if the command block should execute on the first tick, AKA as soon as the
command block is enabled.

FilteredName is a filtered version of Name with all the profanity removed. The client will use this
over Name if this field is not empty and they have the "Filter Profanity" setting enabled.

LastOutput is the output of the last command executed by the command block. It may be left empty to
show simply no output at all, in combination with setting ShouldTrackOutput to false.

Name is the name of the command block updated. If not empty, it will show this name hovering above the
command block when hovering over the block with the cursor.

TickDelay is the delay in ticks between executions of a command block, if it is a repeating command
block.

ShouldTrackOutput specifies if the command block tracks output. If set to false, the output box won't
be shown within the command block.

CommandOrigin holds data that identifies the origin of the requesting of a command. It holds several
fields that may be used to get specific information.
When sent in a CommandRequest packet, the same CommandOrigin should be sent in a CommandOutput packet.

RequestID is an ID that identifies the request of the client. The server should send a CommandOrigin
with the same request ID to ensure it can be matched with the request by the caller of the command.
This is especially important for websocket servers and it seems that this field is only non-empty for
these websocket servers.
UUID is a unique identifier for every instantiation of a command.

CommandOutputMessage represents a message sent by a command that holds the output of one of the commands
executed.

Message is the message that is sent to the client in the chat window. It may either be simply a
message or a translated built-in string like 'commands.tp.success.coordinates', combined with specific
parameters below.

Parameters is a list of parameters that serve to supply the message sent with additional information,
such as the position that a player was teleported to or the effect that was applied to an entity.
These parameters only apply for the Minecraft built-in command output.

Success indicates if the output message was one of a successful command execution. If set to true, the
output message is by default coloured white, whereas if set to false, the message is by default
coloured red.

CommandOutput is sent by the server to the client to send text as output of a command. Most servers do not
use this packet and instead simply send Text packets, but there is reason to send it.
If the origin of a CommandRequest packet is not the player itself, but, for example, a websocket server,
sending a Text packet will not do what is expected: The message should go to the websocket server, not to
the client's chat. The CommandOutput packet will make sure the messages are relayed to the correct origin
of the command request.

CommandRequest is sent by the client to request the execution of a server-side command. Although some
servers support sending commands using the Text packet, this packet is guaranteed to have the correct
result.

Command is the raw entered command line. The client does no parsing of the command line by itself
(unlike it did in the early stages), but lets the server do that.

IsInternal specifies if the command request internal. Setting it to false seems to work and the usage of
this field is not known.

Origin is the data specifying the origin of the command. In other words, the source that the
command was from, such as the player itself or a websocket server.
Version is the version of the command that is being executed. This field currently has no purpose or functionality.

CompletedUsingItem is sent by the server to tell the client that it should be done using the item it is
currently using.

ItemID is the item ID of the item that the client completed using. This should typically be the
ID of the item held in the hand.

ItemUseMethod is the method of the using of the item that was completed. It is one of the constants that
may be found above.
ConeShape represents a cone debug shape.
Height is the height of the cone.
NumSegments is the number of segments used for the cone.
Radii are the radii along the X/Z axes of the cone base.

ContainerClose is sent by the server to close a container the player currently has opened, which was opened
using the ContainerOpen packet, or by the client to tell the server it closed a particular container, such
as the crafting grid.

WindowID is the ID representing the window of the container that should be closed. It must be equal to
the one sent in the ContainerOpen packet to close the designated window.

ContainerType is the type of container that the server is trying to close. This is used to validate on
the client side whether or not the server's close request is valid.

ServerSide determines whether or not the container was force-closed by the server. If this value is
not set correctly, the client may ignore the packet and respond with a PacketViolationWarning.

ContainerOpen is sent by the server to open a container client-side. This container must be physically
present in the world, for the packet to have any effect. Unlike Java Edition, Bedrock Edition requires that
chests for example must be present and in range to open its inventory.

WindowID is the ID representing the window that is being opened. It may be used later to close the
container using a ContainerClose packet.

ContainerType is the type ID of the container that is being opened when opening the container at the
position of the packet. It depends on the block/entity, and could, for example, be the window type of
a chest or a hopper, but also a horse inventory.

ContainerPosition is the position of the container opened. The position must point to a block entity
that actually has a container. If that is not the case, the window will not be opened and the packet
will be ignored, if a valid ContainerEntityUniqueID has not also been provided.

ContainerEntityUniqueID is the unique ID of the entity container that was opened. It is only used if
the ContainerType is one that points to an entity, for example a horse.

ContainerRegistryCleanup is sent by the server to trigger a client-side cleanup of the dynamic container
registry.

RemovedContainers is a list of protocol.FullContainerName's that should be removed from the client-side
container registry.

ContainerSetData is sent by the server to update specific data of a single container, meaning a block such
as a furnace or a brewing stand. This data is usually used by the client to display certain features
client-side.

WindowID is the ID of the window that should have its data set. The player must have a window open with
the window ID passed, or nothing will happen.

Key is the key of the property. It is one of the constants that can be found above. Multiple properties
share the same key, but the functionality depends on the type of the container that the data is set to.
Value is the value of the property. Its use differs per property.

CorrectPlayerMovePrediction is sent by the server if and only if StartGame.ServerAuthoritativeMovementMode
is set to AuthoritativeMovementModeServerWithRewind. The packet is used to correct movement at a specific
point in time.
OnGround specifies if the player was on the ground at the time of the tick below.

Position is the position that the player is supposed to be at the tick written in the field below.
The client will change its current position based on movement after that tick starting from the
Position.
Delta is the change in position compared to what the client sent as its position at that specific tick.
PredictionType is the type of prediction that was corrected. It is one of the constants above.
Rotation is the rotation of the player at the tick written in the field below.
Tick is the tick of the movement which was corrected by this packet.
VehicleAngularVelocity is the angular velocity of the vehicle that the rider is riding.

CraftingData is sent by the server to let the client know all crafting data that the server maintains. This
includes shapeless crafting, crafting table recipes, furnace recipes etc. Each crafting station's recipes
are included in it.

ClearRecipes indicates if all recipes currently active on the client should be cleaned. Doing this
means that the client will have no recipes active by itself: Any CraftingData packets previously sent
will also be discarded, and only the recipes in this CraftingData packet will be used.

ContainerMixes is a list of all recipes to convert a potion from one type to another,
such as from a drinkable potion to a splash potion, or from a splash potion to a lingering potion.
MaterialReducers is a list of all material reducers which is used in education edition chemistry.
PotionMixes is a list of all potion mixing recipes which may be used in the brewing stand.
ShapedRecipes through SmithingTrimRecipes are the typed recipe vectors used by protocol 2168.

CreatePhoto is a packet that allows players to export photos from their portfolios into items in their inventory.
This packet only works on the Education Edition version of Minecraft.
ItemName is the name of the photo as an item.
PhotoName is the name of the photo.
EntityUniqueID is the unique ID of the entity.

CreativeContent is a packet sent by the server to set the creative inventory's content for a player.
Introduced in 1.16, this packet replaces the previous method - sending an InventoryContent packet with
creative inventory window ID.
As of v1.21.60, this packet is no longer required to be sent as part of the login sequence however the
client will crash if they try to open their creative inventory before receiving this packet. Every item
must be part of a group, any items that are not part of a group will need to reference an "anonymous group"
which has an empty name OR no icon. The order of Groups and Items is how the client will render items
in the creative inventory compared to the previous, hard coded order.

Below is an example of defining 2 ungrouped items, 2 grouped items and then another 2 ungrouped items, all
in the nature category.

	CreativeContent{
		Groups: []protocol.CreativeGroup{
			{Category: 1}, // No name or icon, this is the "anonymous group"
			{Category: 1, Name: "itemGroup.name.planks", Icon: protocol.ItemStack{...}}, // A "planks" group
			{Category: 1}, // Another "anonymous group"
		},
		Items: []protocol.CreativeItem{
			{CreativeItemNetworkID: 0, Item: protocol.ItemStack{...}, GroupIndex: 0}, // Ungrouped before "planks"
			{CreativeItemNetworkID: 1, Item: protocol.ItemStack{...}, GroupIndex: 0}, // Ungrouped before "planks"
			{CreativeItemNetworkID: 2, Item: protocol.ItemStack{...}, GroupIndex: 1}, // Grouped under the "planks" group
			{CreativeItemNetworkID: 3, Item: protocol.ItemStack{...}, GroupIndex: 1}, // Grouped under the "planks" group
			{CreativeItemNetworkID: 4, Item: protocol.ItemStack{...}, GroupIndex: 2}, // Ungrouped after "planks"
			{CreativeItemNetworkID: 5, Item: protocol.ItemStack{...}, GroupIndex: 2}, // Ungrouped after "planks"
		}
	}
Entries is a list of the items that should be added to the creative inventory.
Groups is a list of the groups that should be added to the creative inventory.

CreativeGroup represents a group of items in the creative inventory. Each group has a category, name and an
icon that represents the group.
CreativeCategory is the category the group falls under. It is one of the constants above.
GroupIconItem is the item that represents the group in the creative inventory.
Name is the locale name of the group, i.e. "itemGroup.name.planks".

CurrentStructureFeature is sent by the server to let the client know the name of the structure feature
that the player is currently occupying.

CurrentStructureFeature is the identifier of the structure feature that the player is currently occupying.
If the player is not occupying any structure feature, this field is empty.
CylinderShape represents a cylinder debug shape.
Height is the height of the cylinder.
NumSegments is the number of segments used for the cylinder.
RadiusX is the radius of the cylinder along the X axis.
RadiusZ is the radius of the cylinder along the Z axis.

DeathInfo is a packet sent from the server to the client expected to be sent when a player dies. It contains messages
related to the player's death, which are shown on the death screen as of v1.19.10.
DeathCauseAttackName is the cause of the player's death, such as "suffocation" or "suicide".
DeathCauseMessageList is a list of death messages to be shown on the death screen.

DebugInfo is a packet sent by the server to the client. It does not seem to do anything when sent to the
normal client in 1.16.
PlayerUniqueID is the unique ID of the player that the packet is sent to.
Data is the debug data.

DimensionData is a packet sent from the server to the client containing information about data-driven dimensions
that the server may have registered. This packet does not seem to be sent by default, rather only being sent when
any data-driven dimensions are registered.
Definitions contain a list of data-driven dimension definitions registered on the server.

DimensionDefinition contains information specifying dimension-specific properties, used for data-driven dimensions.
These include the range (the height min/max), generator variant, and more.
DefaultBiome is the identifier of the biome that the dimension defaults to.

DimensionType is the numeric identifier of the dimension. This cannot override a vanilla dimension (0-2), but
custom dimensions should start from 1000 like vanilla.

Generator is the variant of generator that exists in the provided dimension. These can be one of the constants
defined above. If this is set to GeneratorLegacy, the legacy horizontal world limits will be enforced.

HeightRange is the number of blocks above MinimumY that exist in the dimension, so that the highest Y
coordinate in the dimension is MinimumY + HeightRange.
MinimumY is the lowest Y coordinate that exists in the dimension.
PackID is the UUID of the behaviour pack which has added the dimension.

Disconnect may be sent by the server to disconnect the client using an optional message to send as the
disconnect screen.

Reason is the reason for the disconnection. This affects the error code displayed on the Ore UI
disconnection screen and is one of the constants above.
NoiseAlignment represents the way the noise of an environment attribute transition is aligned.
EntityDiagnosticTimingInfo represents diagnostics for a specific entity type.
Dimension is the name of the dimension that the entity being timed is in.
DisplayName is the name to display for this timing entry.
Entity is the identifier of the entity that is being timed.
PercentOfTotal is the percentage of time that this timing entry has used compared to others.
Position is the position of the entity that is being timed.
DurationNanos is whole long the timing entry has lasted, in nanoseconds.
SystemCategory maps a diagnostics category name to a system index.
SystemDiagnosticTimingInfo represents diagnostics for a specific system index.
DisplayName is the name to display for this timing entry.
PercentOfTotal is the percentage of time that this timing entry has used compared to others.
SystemIndex is the index of the system that is being timed.
DurationNanos is whole long the timing entry has lasted, in nanoseconds.

EditorNetwork is a packet sent from the server to the client and vise-versa to communicate editor-mode related
information. It carries a single compound tag containing the relevant information.
Payload is a network little endian compound tag holding data relevant to the editor.
RouteToManager ...

EducationSharedResourceURI is an education edition feature that is used for transmitting
education resource settings to clients. It contains a button name and a link URL.
ButtonName is the button name of the resource URI.
LinkURI is the link URI for the resource URI.

CanResizeCodeBuilder specifies if clients connected to the world should be able to resize the code
builder when it is opened.

CodeBuilderDefaultURI is the default URI that the code builder is ran on. Using this, a Code Builder program can
make code directly affect the server.
CodeBuilderTitle is the title of the code builder shown when connected to the CodeBuilderDefaultURI.
DisableLegacyTitleBar ...
ExternalLinkSettings ...
PostProcessFilter ...

EducationSettings is a packet sent by the server to update Minecraft: Education Edition related settings.
It is unused by the normal base game.
EllipsoidShape represents an ellipsoid debug shape.
Radii are the radii of the ellipsoid along the X, Y and Z axes.
SegmentsPerAxis is the number of segments used per axis for the ellipsoid.

EmoteList is sent by the client every time it joins the server and when it equips new emotes. It may be
used by the server to find out which emotes the client has available. If the player has no emotes equipped,
this packet is not sent.
Under certain circumstances, this packet is also sent from the server to the client, but I was unable to
find when this is done.
EmotePieces is a list of emote pieces that the player with the runtime ID above has.

PlayerRuntimeID is the runtime ID of the player that owns the emote pieces below. If sent by the
client, this player runtime ID is always that of the player itself.

Emote is sent by both the server and the client. When the client sends an emote, it sends this packet to
the server, after which the server will broadcast the packet to other players online.

EntityRuntimeID is the entity that sent the emote. When a player sends this packet, it has this field
set as its own entity runtime ID.
EmoteID is the ID of the emote to send.
EmoteLength is the number of ticks that the emote lasts for.

Flags is a combination of flags that change the way the Emote packet operates. When the server sends
this packet to other players, EmoteFlagServerSide must be present.

PlatformID is an identifier only set for particular platforms when using an emote (presumably only for Nintendo
Switch). It is otherwise an empty string, and is used to decide which players are able to emote with each other.

Xuid is the Xbox User ID of the player that sent the emote. It is only set when the emote is used by a player that
is authenticated with Xbox Live.

EnchantmentInstance represents a single enchantment instance with the type of the enchantment and its
level.
EducationExternalLinkSettings ...
DisplayName is the display name in game.
URL is the external link URL.

FeatureRegistry is a packet used to notify the client about the world generation features the server is currently
using. This is used in combination with the client-side world generation system introduced in v1.19.20, allowing the
client to completely generate the chunks of the world without having to rely on the server.
FeaturesDataList is a slice of all registered world generation features.
FullContainerName contains information required to identify a container in a StackRequestSlotInfo.
ContainerName is the ID of the container that the slot was in.

DynamicID is the ID of the container if it is dynamic. If the container is not dynamic, this
field should be left empty. A non-optional value of 0 is assumed to be non-empty.
FurnaceOptions holds the options that a player has selected in a furnace-like container's UI.
Filtering is whether the player has enabled the filtering between recipes they have unlocked or not.
Layout is the layout of the furnace UI. It is one of the FurnaceLayout constants above.

LeftFurnaceTab is the tab that is selected on the left side of the furnace UI. It is one of the
FurnaceLeftTab constants above.
GameRule contains game rule data.
RuleCanBeModified specifies if the game rule can be modified by the player through the in-game UI.
RuleName is the name of the game rule.

RuleValue is the new value of the game rule. This is either a bool, uint32 or float32, or nil for the null
variant, which carries no value at all.

GameRulesChanged is sent by the server to the client to update client-side game rules, such as game rules
like the 'showCoordinates' game rule.
GameRule contains game rule data.
