UUID is a UUID identifying the recipe. Since the CraftingEvent packet no longer exists, this can always be empty.
Width is the width of the recipe's shape.

ShapelessRecipe is a recipe that has no particular shape. Its functionality is shared with the
RecipeShulkerBox and RecipeShapelessChemistry types.
Priority ...

RecipeID is a unique ID of the recipe. This ID must be unique amongst all other types of recipes too,
but its functionality is not exactly known.
UUID is a UUID identifying the recipe. Since the CraftingEvent packet no longer exists, this can always be empty.
FloatRange is an inclusive minimum/maximum pair of float32 values.
Max is the maximum value of the range.
Min is the minimum value of the range.
CameraAimAssistCategory is an aim assist category that defines priorities for specific blocks and entities.
Name is the name of the category which can be used by a CameraAimAssistPreset.

Priorities represents the block and entity specific priorities as well as the default priorities for
this category.

CameraAimAssistPriorities represents the block and entity specific priorities for targetting. The aim
assist will select the block or entity with the highest priority within the specified thresholds.
BlockDefault is the default priority for blocks.
BlockTags is a list of priorities for specific block tags.
Blocks is a list of priorities for specific block identifiers.
Entities is a list of priorities for specific entity identifiers.
EntityDefault is the default priority for entities.
EntityTypeFamilies is a list of priorities for specific entity type families.
CameraSplineDefinition represents a named camera spline definition.
ControlPoints is a list of points that define the spline curve.
Name is the name of the spline definition.
ProgressKeyFrames is a list of progress key frames for the spline.
RotationKeyFrames is a list of rotation key frames for the spline.
SplineType is the optional spline interpolation type.
TotalTime is the total time for the spline animation.
NoiseDescriptor describes the gradient noise used by a BiomeNoiseGradientSurface.
Amplitudes is a list of amplitude values used by the noise. It must contain between 1 and 100 entries.
FirstOctave is the first octave used by the noise.
Name is the string used to initialise the noise.
CameraPreset represents a basic preset that can be extended upon by more complex instructions.
AimAssist defines the aim assist to use when using this preset.

ApplyInheritedStartingRotation specifies if the camera should start at the rotation of the preset it
inherits from, rather than at StartingRotation.
TrackingRadius is the radius around the camera that the aim assist should track targets.
ContinueTargeting determines whether the camera should continue targeting when using aim assist.

ControlScheme is the control scheme that the client should use in this camera. It is one of the following:
 - ControlSchemeLockedPlayerRelativeStrafe is the default behaviour, this cannot be set when the client
   is in a custom camera.
 - ControlSchemeCameraRelative makes movement relative to the camera's transform, with the client's
   rotation being relative to the client's movement.
 - ControlSchemeCameraRelativeStrafe makes movement relative to the camera's transform, with the
   client's rotation being locked.
 - ControlSchemePlayerRelative makes movement relative to the player's transform, meaning holding
   left/right will make the player turn in a circle.
 - ControlSchemePlayerRelativeStrafe makes movement the same as the default behaviour, but can be
   used in a custom camera.
EntityOffset controls the offset from the entity that the camera should be rendered at.
HorizontalRotationLimit is the horizontal rotation limit of the camera.
Parent is the name of the preset that this preset extends upon. This can be left empty.

AudioListener defines where the audio should be played from when using this preset. This is one of the
constants above.
Name is the name of the preset. Each preset must have their own unique name.
PlayerEffects is currently unknown.
PosX is the default X position of the camera.
PosY is the default Y position of the camera.
PosZ is the default Z position of the camera.

Radius is only used in a follow_orbit camera and controls how far away from the player the camera should
be rendered.
RotX is the default pitch of the camera.
RotY is the default yaw of the camera.
RotationSpeed is the speed at which the camera should rotate.
SnapToTarget determines whether the camera should snap to the target entity or not.
StartingRotation is the rotation that the camera starts at when the preset is applied.
VerticalRotationLimit is the vertical rotation limit of the camera.

ViewOffset is only used in a follow_orbit camera and controls an offset based on a pivot point to the
player, causing it to be shifted in a certain direction.
MaxYawLimit is the maximum yaw limit of the camera.
MinYawLimit is the minimum yaw limit of the camera.

ShowCredits is sent by the server to show the Minecraft credits screen to the client. It is typically sent
when the player beats the ender dragon and leaves the End.

StatusType is the status type of the credits. It is one of the constants above, and either starts or
stops the credits.

PlayerRuntimeID is the entity runtime ID of the player to show the credits to. It's not clear why this
field is actually here in the first place.
ShowProfile is sent by the server to show the XBOX Live profile of one player to another.

PlayerXUID is the XBOX Live User ID of the player whose profile should be shown to the player. If it is not
a valid XUID, the client ignores the packet.

ShowStoreOffer is sent by the server to show a Marketplace store offer to a player. It opens a window
client-side that displays the item.
The ShowStoreOffer packet only works on the partnered servers: Servers that are not partnered will not have
a store buttons show up in the in-game pause menu and will, as a result, not be able to open store offers
on the client side. Sending the packet does therefore not work when using a proxy that is not connected to
with the domain of one of the partnered servers.
OfferID is a UUID that identifies the offer for which a window should be opened.

Type is the type of the store offer that is being shown to the player. It is one of the constants that may be
found above.

SimpleEvent is used for enabling or disabling commands and for unlocking world template settings
(both unlocking UI buttons on client and the actual setting on the server).
This is fired from the client to the server and a SetCommandsEnabled is sent back when enabling commands.
EventType is the type of the event to be called. It is one of the constants that may be found above.
SimulationType is an in-progress packet. We currently do not know the use case.
SimType is the simulation type selected.

SmithingTransformRecipe is a recipe specifically used for smithing tables. It has three input items and adds them
together, resulting in a new item.

RecipeID is a unique ID of the recipe. This ID must be unique amongst all other types of recipes too,
but its functionality is not exactly known.
Result is the resulting item from the two items being added together.
SmithingTrimRecipe is a recipe specifically used for applying armour trims to an armour piece inside a smithing table.

RecipeID is a unique ID of the recipe. This ID must be unique amongst all other types of recipes too,
but its functionality is not exactly known.

SpawnExperienceOrb is sent by the server to spawn an experience orb entity client-side. Much like the
AddPainting packet, it is one of the few packets that spawn an entity without using the AddActor packet.

Position is the position to spawn the experience orb on. If the entity is on a distance that the player
cannot see it, the entity will still show up if the player moves closer.

XPValue is the amount of experience in experience points that the orb carries. The client-side
size of the orb depends on the amount of experience in the orb: There are 11 possible sizes for the
orb, for 1–2, 3–6, 7–16, 17–36, 37–72, 73–148, 149–306, 307–616, 617–1236, 1237–2476, and 2477 and up.

SpawnParticleEffect is sent by the server to spawn a particle effect client-side. Unlike other packets that
result in the appearing of particles, this packet can show particles that are not hardcoded in the client.
They can be added and changed through behaviour packs to implement custom particles.

EntityUniqueID is the unique ID of the entity that the spawned particle may be attached to. If this ID
is not -1, the Position below will be interpreted as relative to the position of the entity associated
with this unique ID.

Dimension is the dimension that the particle is spawned in. Its exact usage is not clear, as the
dimension has no direct effect on the particle.

ParticleName is the name of the particle that should be shown. This name may point to a particle effect
that is built-in, or to one implemented by behaviour packs.

MoLangVariables is an encoded JSON map of MoLang variables that may be applicable to the particle spawn. This can
just be left empty in most cases.

Position is the position that the particle should be spawned at. If the position is too far away from
the player, it will not show up.
If EntityUniqueID is not -1, the position will be relative to the position of the entity.

StartGame is sent by the server to send information about the world the player will be spawned in. It
contains information about the position the player spawns in, and information about the world in general
such as its game rules.

EnchantmentSeed is the seed used to seed the random used to produce enchantments in the enchantment
table. Note that the exact correct random implementation must be used to produce the correct results
both client- and server-side.

EntityUniqueID is the unique ID of the player. The unique ID is a value that remains consistent across
different sessions of the same world, but most servers simply fill the runtime ID of the entity out for
this field.

Trial specifies if the world was a trial world, meaning features are limited and there is a time limit
on the world.
Time is the total time that has elapsed since the start of the world.
LevelID is a base64 encoded world ID that is used to identify the world.

MultiplayerCorrelationID is a unique ID specifying the multi-player session of the player. A random
UUID should be filled out for this field.

PlayerPosition is the spawn position of the player in the world. In servers this is often the same as
the world's spawn position found below.

EntityRuntimeID is the runtime ID of the player. The runtime ID is unique for each world session, and
entities are generally identified in packets using this runtime ID.

ClientSideGeneration is true if the client should use the features registered in the FeatureRegistry packet to
generate terrain client-side to save on bandwidth.

TemplateContentIdentity is a UUID specific to the premium world template that might have been used to
generate the world. Servers should always fill out an empty string for this.

WorldTemplateID is a UUID that identifies the template that was used to generate the world. Servers that do not
use a world based off of a template can set this to an empty UUID.

StopSound is sent by the server to stop a sound playing to the player, such as a playing music disk track
or other long-lasting sounds.

SoundName is the name of the sound that should be stopped from playing. If no sound with this name is
currently active, the packet is ignored.

StopAllSounds specifies if all sounds currently playing to the player should be stopped. If set to true, the
SoundName field may be left empty.
StopMusicLegacy is currently unknown.

StructureBlockUpdate is sent by the client when it updates a structure block using the in-game UI. The
data it contains depends on the type of structure block that it is. In Minecraft Bedrock Edition v1.11,
there is only the Export structure block type, but in v1.13 the ones present in Java Edition will,
according to the wiki, be added too.
Position is the position of the structure block that is updated.
Waterlogged specifies if non-air blocks replace water or combine with water.

ShouldTrigger specifies if the structure block should be triggered immediately after this packet
reaches the server.

StructureSettings is a struct holding settings of a structure block. Its fields may be changed using the
in-game UI on the client-side.
AnimationMode ...
AnimationDuration ...

Seed is the seed used to omit blocks if Integrity is not equal to one. If the Seed is 0, a random
seed is selected to omit blocks.

Integrity is usually 1, but may be set to a number between 0 and 1 to omit blocks randomly, using
the Seed that follows.

LastEditingPlayerUniqueID is the unique ID of the player that last edited the structure block that
these settings concern.

Mirror specifies the way the structure should be mirrored. It is either no mirror at all, mirror on the
x/z axis or both.

Rotation is the rotation that the structure block should obtain. See the constants above for available
options.
Pivot is the pivot around which the structure may be rotated.

entries.field: Should Allow Non Ticking Player and Ticking Area Chunks
entries.doc:
AllowNonTickingChunks specifies if the structure should allow non-ticking chunks. If set to false, the structure
will export non-ticking chunks.

IgnoreBlocks specifies if the structure should ignore blocks or include them. If set to false, blocks
will show up in the exported structure.

IgnoreEntities specifies if the structure should ignore entities or include them. If set to false,
entities will also show up in the exported structure.

Offset is the offset position that was set in the structure block. The area exported is offset by this
position.

PaletteName is the name of the palette used in the structure. Currently, it seems that this field is
always 'default'.

Size is the size of the area that is about to be exported. The area exported will start at the
Position + Offset, and will extend as far as Size specifies.
StructureTemplateDataRequest is sent by the client to request data of a structure.

RequestedOperation specifies the type of template data request that the player sent. It is one of the
constants found above.

StructureName is the name of the structure that was set in the structure block's UI. This is the name
used to export the structure to a file.
StructurePosition is the position of the structure block that has its template data requested.

StructureSettings is a struct of settings that should be used for exporting the structure. These settings are
identical to the last sent in the StructureBlockUpdate packet by the client.

StructureTemplateDataResponse is sent by the server to send data of a structure to the client in response
to a StructureTemplateDataRequest packet.

ResponseType specifies the response type of the packet. This depends on the RequestType field sent in
the StructureTemplateDataRequest packet and is one of the constants above.

StructureName is the name of the structure that was requested. This is the name used to export the
structure to a file.
SubChunk sends data about multiple sub-chunks around a center point.
CacheEnabled is whether the sub-chunk caching is enabled or not.

SubChunkPos is the position of a sub-chunk. The X and Z coordinates are the coordinates of the chunk, and the Y
coordinate is the absolute sub-chunk index.
SubChunkRequest requests specific sub-chunks from the server using a center point.

SubClientLogin is sent when a sub-client joins the server while another client is already connected to it.
The packet is sent as a result of split-screen game play, and allows up to four players to play using the
same network connection. After an initial Login packet from the 'main' client, each sub-client that
connects sends a SubClientLogin to request their own login.

ConnectionRequest is a string containing information about the player and JWTs that may be used to
verify if the player is connected to XBOX Live. The connection request also contains the necessary
client public key to initiate encryption.
The ConnectionRequest in this packet is identical to the one found in the Login packet.
SyncActorProperty is an alternative to synced actor data.
PropertyData ...
SyncWorldClockStateData represents the state data for synchronising a world clock.
ClockID is the unique identifier for the clock.
IsPaused indicates if the clock is paused.
Time is the current time of the clock.
SyncWorldClocks is sent by the server to initialise and synchronise world clocks with the client.

PlayerMovementSettings represents the different server authoritative movement settings. These control how
the client will provide input to the server.
RewindHistorySize is the amount of history to keep at maximum.

ServerAuthoritativeBlockBreaking specifies if block breaking should be sent through
packet.PlayerAuthInput or not.

TakeItemActor is sent by the server when a player picks up an item entity. It makes the item entity
disappear to viewers and shows the pick-up animation.

TakerEntityRuntimeID is the runtime ID of the entity that took the item, which is usually a player, but
could be another entity like a zombie too.

ItemEntityRuntimeID is the entity runtime ID of the item that is being taken by another entity. It will
disappear to viewers after showing the pick-up animation.
TextShape represents a text debug shape.
BackgroundColor is the RGBA colour to use for the text background. This is a translucent black colour by default.
DepthTest is whether the text should show through walls. Use true for default behaviour.

LineGapHeight is the gap to leave between each line of multiline text. If not set, the client uses its
default gap.

ShowBackface is if the background should render on the back side of the shape. This only has a visible effect when
UseRotation is true since you cannot see the back side of the text otherwise. Use true for default behaviour.

ShowTextBackface is if the text should render on the back side of the shape. This only has a visible effect when
UseRotation is true since you cannot see the back side of the text otherwise. Use true for default behaviour.
Text is the text of the debug text shape.

UseRotation is if the text should use the provided rotation, meaning it will be static and does not follow the
camera. Use false for default behaviour.

Text is sent by the client to the server to send chat messages, and by the server to the client to forward
or send messages, which may be chat, popups, tips etc.

FilteredMessage is a filtered version of Message with all the profanity removed. The client will use
this over Message if this field is not empty and they have the "Filter Profanity" setting enabled.

XUID is the XBOX Live user ID of the player that sent the message. It is only set for packets of
TextTypeChat. When sent to a player, the player will only be shown the chat message if a player with
this XUID is present in the player list and not muted, or if the XUID is empty.
TickingAreasLoadStatus is sent by the server to the client to notify the client of a ticking area's loading status.
WaitingForPreload is true if the server is waiting for the area's preload.
TimeMarkerData represents a time marker within a world clock.
ID is the unique identifier for the time marker.
Name is the name of the time marker.
Period is the optional period for the time marker.
Time is the time at which the marker is set.

ToastRequest is a packet sent from the server to the client to display a toast to the top of the screen. These toasts
are the same as the ones seen when, for example, loading a new resource pack or obtaining an achievement.
Content is the message that the toast may contain alongside the title.
Title is the title of the toast.

Transfer is sent by the server to transfer a player from the current server to another. Doing so will
fully disconnect the client, bring it back to the main menu and make it connect to the next server.
GatheringsConfiguration optionally identifies the gathering being joined on the target server.
ReloadWorld currently has an unknown usage.
ServerAddress is the address of the new server, which might be either a hostname or an actual IP address.
ServerPort is the UDP port of the new server.

TrimData is sent by the server to the client when they first join the server. It contains a list of all the patterns
and materials that can be applied via armour trims.

TrimMaterialList is a list of materials that can be applied to armour. These are mostly different ores that have different
colours for more customization.

TrimPatternList is a list of patterns that can be applied to armour. Each pattern has its own style and texture that is
defined through resource packs.
TrimMaterial represents a material that can be used when applying an armour trim.
Color is the colour code used for text formatting, for example '§j'.
ItemName is the identifier of the item that represents the material, for example, 'minecraft:netherite_ingot'.
MaterialID is the identifier of the material, for example 'netherite'.
TrimPattern represents a pattern that can be applied to an armour piece in combination with a TrimMaterial.

ItemName is the identifier of the item that represents the pattern, for example
'minecraft:wayfinder_armor_trim_smithing_template'.
PatternID is the identifier of the pattern, for example, 'wayfinder'.

UnlockedRecipes gives the client a list of recipes that have been unlocked, restricting the recipes that appear in
the recipe book.

UnlockType is the type of unlock that the packet represents, and can either be adding or removing a list of recipes.
It is one of the constants listed above.
Recipes is a list of recipe names that have been unlocked.

UpdateAbilities is a packet sent from the server to the client to update the abilities of the player. It, along with
the UpdateAdventureSettings packet, are replacements of the AdventureSettings packet since v1.19.10.
Data represents various data about the abilities of a player, such as ability layers or permissions.

UpdateAdventureSettings is a packet sent from the server to the client to update the adventure settings of the player.
It, along with the UpdateAbilities packet, are replacements of the AdventureSettings packet since v1.19.10.

UpdateAttributes is sent by the server to update an amount of attributes of any entity in the world. These
attributes include ones such as the health or the movement speed of the entity.

Attributes is a slice of new attributes that the entity gets. It includes attributes such as its
health, movement speed, etc. Note that only changed attributes have to be sent in this packet. It is
not required to send attributes that did not have their values changed.

EntityRuntimeID is the runtime ID of the entity. The runtime ID is unique for each world session, and
entities are generally identified in packets using this runtime ID.
Tick is the server tick at which the packet was sent. It is used in relation to CorrectPlayerMovePrediction.

UpdateBlock is sent by the server to update a block client-side, without resending the entire chunk that
the block is located in. It is particularly useful for small modifications like block breaking/placing.
BlockPosition is the block position at which a block is updated.

BlockRuntimeID is the runtime ID of the block that is placed at Position after sending the packet
to the client.

Flags is a combination of flags that specify the way the block is updated client-side. It is a
combination of the flags above, but typically sending only the BlockUpdateNetwork flag is sufficient.

Layer is the world layer on which the block is updated. For most blocks, this is the first layer, as
that layer is the default layer to place blocks on, but for blocks inside of each other, this differs.

UpdateBlockSynced is sent by the server to synchronise the falling of a falling block entity with the
transitioning back and forth from and to a solid block. It is used to prevent the entity from flickering,
and is used in places such as the pushing of blocks with pistons.

ActorSyncMessage is the type of the transition that happened. It is either BlockToEntityTransition, when
a block placed becomes a falling entity, or EntityToBlockTransition, when a falling entity hits the
ground and becomes a solid block again.
BlockPosition is the block position at which a block is updated.

BlockRuntimeID is the runtime ID of the block that is placed at Position after sending the packet
to the client.

Flags is a combination of flags that specify the way the block is updated client-side. It is a
combination of the flags above, but typically sending only the BlockUpdateNetwork flag is sufficient.

Layer is the world layer on which the block is updated. For most blocks, this is the first layer, as
that layer is the default layer to place blocks on, but for blocks inside of each other, this differs.

UniqueActorID is the unique ID of the falling block entity that the block transitions to or that the
entity transitions from.
Note that for both possible values for TransitionType, the EntityUniqueID should point to the falling
block entity involved.

UpdateClientInputLocks is sent by the server to the client to lock specific player inputs such as camera
rotation, movement, jumping, sneaking, mounting or individual directional movement.

InputLockComponentData is a set of flags that specify which client inputs are disabled, such as whether the player can
move, rotate the camera, jump, sneak or mount/dismount entities. It is a combination of the
ClientInputLock constants above.

UpdateClientOptions is sent by the client when some of the client's options are updated, such as the
graphics mode.
FilterProfanityChange is if the client only uses filtered messages or not.
GraphicsModeChange is the graphics mode that the client is using. It is one of the constants above.

UpdateEquip is sent by the server to the client upon opening a horse inventory. It is used to set the
content of the inventory and specify additional properties, such as the items that are allowed to be put
in slots of the inventory.

EntityUniqueID is the unique ID of the entity whose equipment was 'updated' to the player. It is
typically the horse entity that had its inventory opened.

Size is the size of the horse inventory that should be opened. A bigger size does, in fact, change the
amount of slots displayed.

WindowType is the type of the window that was opened. Generally, this is the type of a horse inventory,
as the packet is specifically made for that.

UpdatePlayerGameType is sent by the server to change the game mode of a player. It is functionally
identical to the SetPlayerGameType packet.

GameType is the new game type of the player. It is one of the constants that can be found in
set_player_game_type.go. Some of these game types require additional flags to be set in an
UpdateAbilities packet for the game mode to obtain its full functionality.

PlayerUniqueID is the entity unique ID of the player that should have its game mode updated. If this
packet is sent to other clients with the player unique ID of another player, nothing happens.
Tick is the server tick at which the packet was sent. It is used in relation to CorrectPlayerMovePrediction.

UpdateSoftEnum is sent by the server to update a soft enum, also known as a dynamic enum, previously sent
in the AvailableCommands packet. It is sent whenever the enum should get new options or when some of its
options should be removed.
The UpdateSoftEnum packet will apply for enums that have been set in the AvailableCommands packet with the
'Dynamic' field of the CommandEnum set to true.

EnumName is the type of the enum. This type must be identical to the one set in the AvailableCommands
packet, because the client uses this to recognise which enum to update.

UpdateType is the type of the action to execute on the enum. The Options field has a different result,
depending on what ActionType is used.

Values is a list of options that should be updated. Depending on the ActionType field, either these
options will be added to the enum, the enum options will be set to these options or all of these
options will be removed from the enum.
UpdateSubChunkBlocks is essentially just UpdateBlock packet, however for a set of blocks in a sub-chunk.
Position is the block position of the sub-chunk being referred to.

UpdateTrade is sent by the server to update the trades offered by a villager to a player. It is sent at the
moment that a player interacts with a villager.

DisplayName is the name displayed at the top of the trading UI. It is usually used to represent the
profession of the villager in the UI.

EntityUniqueID is the unique ID of the entity (usually a player) for which the trades are updated. The
updated trades may apply only to this entity.

EntityUniqueID is the unique ID of the entity (usually a player) for which the trades are updated. The
updated trades may apply only to this entity.
Size is the amount of trading options that the villager has.

WindowType is an identifier specifying the type of the window opened. In vanilla, it appears this is
always filled out with 15.
VoxelCells represents a 3D grid of voxel cell data.
Storage is the raw cell data stored in the grid.
XSize is the size of the grid along the X axis.
YSize is the size of the grid along the Y axis.
ZSize is the size of the grid along the Z axis.
VoxelShape represents a voxel shape with cells and coordinate axes.
Cells is the grid of cells representing solid and empty regions.
XCoordinates is a list of X axis coordinates for the shape.
YCoordinates is a list of Y axis coordinates for the shape.
ZCoordinates is a list of Z axis coordinates for the shape.
VoxelShapes is sent by the server to send voxel shape data to the client.
CustomShapeCount is the number of custom shapes.
NameMap is a map of shape names to IDs.
Shapes is a list of voxel shapes.

ServerURI is the URI to make the client connect to. It can be, for example, 'localhost:8000/ws' to
connect to a websocket server on the localhost at port 8000.
WorldClockData represents a complete world clock with its time markers.
ID is the unique identifier for the clock.
IsPaused indicates if the clock is paused.
Name is the name of the clock.
Time is the current time of the clock.
TimeMarkers is a list of time markers for this clock.
ExperimentData holds data on an experiment that is either enabled or disabled.

Enabled specifies if the experiment is enabled. Vanilla typically always sets this to true for any
experiments sent.
Name is the name of the experiment.

ItemDescriptor represents a type of item descriptor. This is one of the concrete types below. It is an alias of
Marshaler.

MapDecoration is a fixed decoration on a map: Its position or other properties do not change automatically
client-side.
PersonaPiece represents a piece of a persona skin. All pieces are sent separately.
